quests.instruction: A child lives 400 metres from school along a quiet pavement. What is the healthiest way to get there?
quests.hint: No ticket, no fuel, and only a few minutes.
quests.explanation: Walking short distances is free, healthy, and often as quick as waiting for a vehicle. It also keeps the roads near school less crowded.
quests.funFact: Even a ten-minute walk each way adds up to a good amount of daily exercise.

quests.instruction: A child lives 8 kilometres from school along a road with no railway. Which shared ride is the best everyday choice?
quests.hint: It picks up many children along a set route.
quests.explanation: A school bus or local bus picks up many children along a route. Walking would take too long, and scooters are not suited to long daily trips.
quests.funFact: School bus drivers follow a set route and timetable each day.

quests.instruction: After an evening club it is dark outside. Which is the safest way to travel home?
quests.hint: There is safety in company.
quests.explanation: Travelling with a trusted adult or friend is safer in the dark. Staying aware of your surroundings, and avoiding loud headphones, helps you notice danger.
quests.funFact: Walking in a group makes you easier for drivers to see.

quests.instruction: Before a flight, which bag should hold your passport and tickets so you can reach them easily?
quests.hint: Keep this one with you, not in the hold.
quests.explanation: Important papers should stay in a small bag you carry yourself. Big suitcases go in the hold, where you cannot reach them during the flight.
quests.funFact: Carry-on bags must fit within size limits set by each airline.

quests.instruction: Many suitcases look alike. What small label with your name and phone number helps lost luggage find its way back to you?
quests.hint: It attaches to the handle.
quests.explanation: A luggage tag shows who a bag belongs to. If a bag is lost, staff can use the tag to contact you.
quests.funFact: Airlines also attach their own paper tag, with a barcode, to checked bags.

quests.instruction: It is a hot day and you have a long bus ride ahead. Which is the best thing to pack?
quests.hint: Your body needs it more when the weather is warm.
quests.explanation: Staying hydrated is important in hot weather, especially if the bus is slow or stuck in traffic.
quests.funFact: People can feel tired and dizzy when they do not drink enough, especially in hot weather.

quests.instruction: Grandparents live 40 kilometres away along a country road with no railway. A family of four wants to visit for the day, taking gifts. Which is the best choice?
quests.hint: Think about which one can use country roads.
quests.explanation: A car can travel country roads door to door and carries people and gifts. Trains need railway lines, and a plane would be far too much for 40 kilometres.
quests.funFact: Experts suggest taking a break from driving about every two hours on long trips.

quests.instruction: It is a very hot day and you need to cross the city. Which is the coolest, most comfortable choice?
quests.hint: It runs in tunnels and many have air conditioning.
quests.explanation: Metro trains are often air-conditioned and shaded underground, so they can be a cool choice in hot weather.
quests.funFact: Many metro stations have fans or air conditioning to keep passengers comfortable.

quests.instruction: A road winds up a hillside and you start to feel sick in the car. What can help?
quests.hint: Look into the distance and get some fresh air.
quests.explanation: Looking out of the window at the distant view helps your eyes and body agree about movement. Reading or looking at a phone can make car sickness worse.
quests.funFact: Many people feel car sickness less when they sit facing forward.

quests.instruction: To catch an early train, which helps you wake up in time?
quests.hint: It rings at the time you set.
quests.explanation: Setting an alarm helps you leave early enough. Arriving a few minutes before departure is much better than rushing.
quests.funFact: Some people set two alarms so they never oversleep.

quests.instruction: Which screen at a station shows whether trains are on time or running late?
quests.hint: It lists times, platforms, and delays.
quests.explanation: Departure screens list train times, platforms, and delays. Checking one tells you where to go and how long to wait.
quests.funFact: Screens at big stations update within seconds when a platform changes.

quests.instruction: Your train is delayed by 30 minutes. Which is a calm, sensible way to pass the time?
quests.hint: Find something quiet to do while you wait.
quests.explanation: Delays happen, and staying calm makes the wait easier. Reading, listening to music, or chatting with family helps the time pass.
quests.funFact: Many stations have waiting rooms with seats and shelter.

quests.instruction: Heavy rain has covered the road ahead with deep, fast-moving water. What is the safest choice?
quests.hint: Never try to cross it.
quests.explanation: Floodwater can hide holes and push vehicles away, even when it looks shallow. The safest choice is to turn back or wait somewhere safe.
quests.funFact: Moving water only 30 centimetres deep can float a car.

quests.instruction: The low sun is shining straight into a driver's eyes. What helps them see?
quests.hint: It shades the eyes.
quests.explanation: Sunglasses reduce glare so drivers can see the road and other vehicles. Many cars also have fold-down visors.
quests.funFact: Sun visors in cars fold down to shade the driver's eyes.

quests.instruction: On a hot sunny day, which of these is dangerous to leave a child or pet inside, even for a few minutes?
quests.hint: Its windows trap heat like a greenhouse.
quests.explanation: A closed car heats up very quickly and can become dangerously hot. Children and pets should never be left inside.
quests.funFact: On a warm day, the inside of a parked car can get far hotter than the air outside in a short time.

quests.instruction: Many station platforms have a coloured line near the edge. Which colour is the line you must stay behind?
quests.hint: It is the colour of a warning light.
quests.explanation: The line tells passengers to stay back from the edge while trains arrive. Standing behind it keeps you safe from moving trains.
quests.funFact: Many platforms also have bumpy tiles so people who cannot see well can feel the edge.

quests.instruction: Which sign marks seats or spaces for people who use wheelchairs or find walking difficult?
quests.hint: It shows a person in a chair with wheels.
quests.explanation: This sign shows reserved places. Leaving them free means the people who need them can travel comfortably.
quests.funFact: This symbol is used around the world.

quests.instruction: What do you press on many buses to tell the driver you want to get off at the next stop?
quests.hint: Press it early so the driver has time to slow down.
quests.explanation: The stop button lights up a sign for the driver. Pressing it early gives the driver time to stop safely at the next stop.
quests.funFact: On some buses you pull a cord instead of pressing a button.

quests.instruction: The school bus leaves at nine o'clock. Which clock shows 9:00?
quests.hint: The short hand points to nine and the long hand points straight up.
quests.explanation: On a clock, the short hand shows the hour and the long hand shows the minutes. At 9:00 the long hand points straight up.
quests.funFact: Timetables often use 24-hour times, so 9:00 pm is written as 21:00.

quests.instruction: The ferry leaves at half past three. Which clock shows 3:30?
quests.hint: Half past means the long hand points to six.
quests.explanation: Half past means thirty minutes after the hour. At 3:30 the short hand sits between three and four.
quests.funFact: Ferries often run on fixed timetables, so being a few minutes early helps.

quests.instruction: A train leaves at 6:00 and the journey takes two hours. Which clock shows when it arrives?
quests.hint: Count forward two hours from six.
quests.explanation: Six plus two is eight, so the train arrives at 8:00. Doing this sum helps you plan pick-ups and meetings.
quests.funFact: Train timetables list both departure and arrival times.

quests.instruction: A friend says, 'Turn left at the bridge.' Which arrow shows that turn?
quests.hint: Face the way you are walking. Left is the side your left hand is on.
quests.explanation: Left and right depend on which way you are facing. A turn left means you change direction toward your left side.
quests.funFact: Giving directions with landmarks, like a bridge or a shop, helps travellers find their way.

quests.instruction: On a map, north is at the top. The station is directly north of you. Which arrow points toward it?
quests.hint: North is toward the top of the map.
quests.explanation: Maps usually have north at the top. A compass or map helps you head the right way.
quests.funFact: A compass needle points toward magnetic north.

quests.instruction: You face north, walk straight, turn right, then turn right again. Which way are you now facing?
quests.hint: Two right turns make half a full turn.
quests.explanation: Each right turn is a quarter turn. Two quarter turns make a half turn, so you face the opposite direction, which is south.
quests.funFact: Sailors and pilots use compass directions like north, south, east, and west.

quests.instruction: Which lets you tap and pay for a bus or metro ride without using cash?
quests.hint: It is a small plastic rectangle.
quests.explanation: Many cities use travel cards or bank cards that you tap on a reader. This is quicker than counting coins.
quests.funFact: Some cities let you pay with a phone as well.

quests.instruction: Which tells passengers the name of the next stop on many buses and trains?
quests.hint: Listen for a voice over the speakers.
quests.explanation: Announcements and screens tell passengers where they are, which helps when you do not know the route.
quests.funFact: Many vehicles use both spoken announcements and screens so everyone can find out the next stop.

quests.instruction: Which helps you stay steady on a standing bus when the driver brakes?
quests.hint: Keep one hand free to hold on.
quests.explanation: Holding a handrail or pole keeps you steady when a bus brakes or turns. Using both hands for a phone makes it easy to fall.
quests.funFact: Buses brake and turn quickly, so even adults hold on.

quests.instruction: Maya walks five minutes to the station, rides 20 minutes underground, then walks five minutes to school. Which vehicle did she ride in the middle?
quests.hint: It was the part of the trip that ran in tunnels.
quests.explanation: Her journey has three parts: walk, ride, walk. Using the metro for the long middle part saves time.
quests.funFact: Most public transport trips begin and end on foot.

quests.instruction: At the weekend, Arun cycles to a lake and hires a boat that he moves with a paddle. Which boat is it?
quests.hint: No motor and no sail, only paddles.
quests.explanation: Paddling moves a canoe without any motor or sail. It is a quiet way to enjoy the water.
quests.funFact: Canoe paddles have flat blades that push plenty of water with each stroke.

quests.instruction: A family drives to the station, takes a train to the coast, and then travels over the water to an island. What carries them across the water?
quests.hint: It is the last stage, and it floats.
quests.explanation: Sometimes a trip uses several types of transport, one after another. Each suits a different part of the journey.
quests.funFact: Some island ferries are timed to connect with train arrivals so passengers can change easily.
